clue.text: One bearing another, losing initial value

parts.note: west, abbreviated W, is one compass bearing

indicators.note: the first letter of that second bearing is dropped from its front

parts.note: north is a second compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone carrying another person loses their early worth, as if a backer were being devalued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bearing' and 'another' are both compass points, not people carrying each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thing's merit or price is its value.

clue.text: Plant's mysterious war secrets

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spy has planted cryptic military secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant's' reads as plant is, a spy's planted secrets in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: watercress is a peppery aquatic plant grown for salads.

clue.text: Modelling once more, taking it easy

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
posing is modelling, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A model is back sitting for the artist, relaxing as she does so.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reposing means resting or lying at ease.

clue.text: He'll shortly go down, I conclude, in the capital

indicators.note: the single letter I comes at the end of the build
the final letter is cut off, making the word short

parts.note: the contraction is written without its apostrophe
to sink is to go down

explanation.surface: A man predicts he will soon be ruined in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: One will not come out with poet for this fish

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to come out on strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A shy creature refusing to emerge, paired with a poet, is asked to name a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' means go on strike here, not emerge. The scabbard fish is a long, silvery sea fish named for its sword-sheath shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the scabbard is a kind of eel-like marine fish.

clue.text: Therefore second unknown article is a bean

parts.note: so means therefore
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, y the second
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A logical chain concluding that some unidentified item is a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: soya is a legume whose seed is the soybean.

clue.text: Clasp relative with impatient expression

parts.note: bro is short for brother
och is a Scots exclamation of irritation

explanation.surface: A sibling hugs you while tutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a brooch is an ornament fastened with a pin or clasp.

clue.text: Dart if misdirected is off course

indicators.note: aimed wrongly, so the letters are sent astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly thrown dart veers wide of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adrift means drifting without control, astray from the intended route.

clue.text: Get some sleep, it's almost twelve

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, its last letter missing

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: Time for a nap: it is nearly midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to doze is to nap lightly.

clue.text: Leading science? It's a branch of geometry

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
an ology is a jocular term for any science

explanation.surface: A question about which discipline leads the field, answered by naming a mathematical branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Topology studies properties of shapes preserved under stretching, a field grown from geometry.

clue.text: Appropriate answer replaced nothing on the other side

indicators.note: the letter A is swapped in where the zero-shaped letter stood

parts.note: opposite means on the other side
nothing is the letter O, like zero

explanation.surface: A fitting reply was substituted for silence across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' names the O that the A ousts, at the head of OPPOSITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something apposite is apt and well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Wilfully doing wrong according to a number of lines

parts.note: per means according to, as in per instructions
a verse is a group of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately sins by the book, line by line.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perverse means contrary, deliberately acting against what is right or expected.

clue.text: Cancel production of 'Cinders'

indicators.note: a production reworks material into new form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre calls off its staging of the pantomime Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' is Cinderella, a pantomime staple in Britain; here it is just letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rescind an order or law is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: From other end remove from position of authority

indicators.note: the answer is made from the following letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Deposing a ruler from the far end of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is an unusual signal: the answer is fashioned from the letters of OTHER END.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dethrone is to depose a monarch or topple a leader.

clue.text: Two spinning bodies had fungus

parts.note: our planet, the Earth, rotates on its axis
a star such as the Sun also rotates

explanation.surface: A pair of rotating objects caught a fungal infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the earthstar is a puffball mushroom whose outer layer splits into a star shape.

clue.text: About to start old wine, limited edition, taken to another realm again

indicators.note: the first piece goes at the beginning

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ex means former or old
port is a fortified wine
ed is the shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: Sounds like a vintner's note on a rare old port bottled in a small run.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: goods re-exported are shipped out again to a foreign country after being imported.

clue.text: Organisation looking after elegant high-rise building?

indicators.note: with a question mark, building suggests the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Which body cares for a stylish tower block?
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the thing cared for, but it signals the rearrangement of ELEGANT HIGH RISE. English Heritage is the charity that manages historic sites in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the charity is an organisation that looks after England's historic monuments and buildings.

clue.text: Heading for frozen water? Stuck in it

parts.note: ice is frozen water
bound means heading for, as in homeward bound

explanation.surface: A ship sailing for icy seas gets trapped there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition points back to the frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an icebound ship is trapped fast in ice.

clue.text: A weapon in catalogue liable to spread fear

indicators.note: the weapon sits inside the catalogue

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gun listed in a catalogue might scare people.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an alarmist needlessly raises fears, so is liable to frighten others.

clue.text: Knowing story about promises to pay

parts.note: a saga is a long story
C, for circa, means about
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A tale wise to the ways of credit notes and debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sagacious person is shrewd and wise, showing knowing judgement.

clue.text: Georgia on the wagon with knight

parts.note: GA is the US postal code for Georgia
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A teetotaller from Georgia rides with a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' looks like the idiom for not drinking; here 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sir Gawain is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Plant different clues round circle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the ring shape
made different, so the letters take another order

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A gardener's word puzzle with altered hints around a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns CLUES into CLEUS, and 'round' wraps those letters about the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: coleus is a decorative plant grown for its colourful leaves.

clue.text: Half of them exclude travel ban

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
go means travel

explanation.surface: Half of a group are barred from journeying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: In France I went before Sam the shopkeeper

indicators.note: the French word comes in front of the surname

parts.note: je is French for I
Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A traveller in France recalls getting ahead of someone named Sam.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a jeweller is a trader who keeps a shop selling gems and rings.

clue.text: Joke book abridged

indicators.note: shortened, so the last two letters are cut

parts.note: Joshua is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A comic tale cut down for a shorter edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to josh is to tease or kid playfully.

clue.text: Ferment dodgy gear

indicators.note: unreliable or faulty, suggesting the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A faulty set of equipment causing unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a noun, ferment means agitation or furious excitement.

clue.text: Get to know Bill Strange in an interesting and curious way

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

parts.words: Strange in an interesting and curious way
parts.note: quaint describes something oddly charming or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Meeting a curious, oddly fascinating man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to acquaint oneself with something is to become familiar with it.

clue.text: Good-looking worker takes part

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: An attractive labourer joins in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a handsome person is attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Old-fashioned tearaway going after appropriate hairstyle

indicators.note: the rebel's three letters follow the hairstyle

parts.note: the DA, or duck's arse, was the quiffed haircut fitting for a Teddy boy
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British young rebel

explanation.surface: A young rebel chases a fashionable haircut that is long out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits; their signature hairdo was the DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dated is out of style, belonging to an earlier time.
